papers.title: Disentanglement of interfacial electric fields and electrochemical potential gradients reveals a multidimensional kinetic landscape
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical reactions occur at solid–liquid interfaces, where the applied electrochemical potential gradient can act as thermodynamic driving force but can also induce interfacial polarization. A key question has long been how local changes in the chemical potentials of the electrons and the associated excess charge and electric fields impact catalyst kinetics. Here we combine temperature-dependent current transients from oxidative CO stripping with a CO coverage-dependent potential of zero total charge and Raman spectroscopy. We observe a reduction of the activation energy with increasing driving force. By contrast, increasing the distance between the applied potential and the potential of zero total charge results in an increase in the apparent activation energy, which we ascribe to an electric field effect in the double layer. More generally, the results demonstrate how interfacial changes in the chemical potentials give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape, in which single-descriptor kinetics fail to capture the nature of the overpotential.
papers.tldr: Combining temperature-dependent CO-stripping transients, potential-of-zero-total-charge measurements, and Raman spectroscopy, this study disentangles double-layer electric-field effects from the applied electrochemical driving force and shows that electrocatalytic kinetics form a multidimensional landscape that single-descriptor overpotential models cannot capture.

papers.title: Influence of dielectric environment on the optical properties of the CVD-grown monolayer WSe2
papers.abstract: Regulating excitonic emission in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors through external perturbations offers an effective route to improving the performance of their optoelectronic devices. Here, we investigate the evolution of exciton and trion emissions in monolayer tungsten diselenide (WSe2) under different dielectric environments using temperature-dependent Raman and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. Through deconvolution of the PL spectra, it is observed that both low temperature and high-dielectric environment facilitate the formation of trions, leading to an increase in their integrated intensity compared with that of the neutral excitons. This phenomenon can be attributed to the higher trion binding energy at low temperature and the dielectric-induced deep-to-shallow transition of defect levels, which modifies the effective charged defect levels in WSe2 and consequently influences the formation and recombination dynamics of the excitons and trions differently. Our results provide deeper insight into the emission mechanisms of excitonic complexes in 2D semiconductors under dielectric environments and offer useful guidance for dielectric engineering of optoelectronic and photonic devices based on transition metal dichalcogenides.
papers.tldr: Low temperature and high-dielectric environments enhance trion formation in CVD-grown monolayer WSe₂ by increasing trion binding energy and shifting defect levels, providing guidance for dielectric engineering of 2D optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Turning Insulators into Accelerators: Deciphering the Interfacial Ionic Conductivity Boost in Composite Solid-State Electrolytes through Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Abstract Halide solid-state electrolytes have emerged as promising candidates for all-solid-state lithium batteries due to their high oxidative stability and deformability, yet their moderate ionic conductivity remains a bottleneck. While incorporating ionically insulating ZrO2 nanoparticles has been experimentally shown to enhance the ionic conductivity of Li2ZrCl6, the atomistic origin governing this interfacial phenomenon remains unclear. Here, we bridge the spatiotemporal gap in modeling complex heterostructures by developing an accurate machine-learned force field based on the neuroevolution potential, enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 heterostructures. By systematically investigating four representative low-lattice-mismatch ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 interfaces, we identify spontaneous interfacial amorphization driven by space-charge effects upon surface cleavage, trapping Li+ and leading to under-coordinated Li+ polyhedra with pronounced geometric distortion. These distorted amorphous interfacial regions exhibit markedly enhanced Li+ hopping activity, significantly outperforming the bulk lattice, provided that the local mobile Li+ density is not depleted by surface charge redistribution. This work establishes a computational framework for training validated machine-learned force fields for interfaces and provides one plausible origin for the experimentally observed conductivity boost in the insulator-conductor composites, guiding the rational design of electrolytes toward next-generation solid-state batteries.
papers.tldr: Machine-learned molecular dynamics reveals that ZrO₂/Li₂ZrCl₆ interfaces spontaneously amorphize via space-charge effects, creating distorted, under-coordinated Li⁺ environments that enhance Li⁺ hopping and explain the conductivity boost—provided surface charge redistribution does not deplete local mobile Li⁺.

papers.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
authors: Yuxin Duan, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Song Luo, Long Zhang, Zhanghai Chen
papers.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.
papers.tldr: The paper realizes dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, showing strongly enhanced exciton–electron binding and orientation-selective many-body dressing controlled by dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization.

papers.title: Evidence of Polarons and Their Ultrafast Optical Undressing in a Topological Semimetal
papers.abstract: Abstract Polarons, formed by coupling electrons with lattice vibrations, are of intense interest in topological semimetals owing to their crucial role in dictating high-speed topological optoelectronics. However, polarons in topological semimetals have thus far been exclusively observed as light-induced transient quasiparticles, leaving equilibrium polarons and their ultrafast dynamics elusive. Here, using time-resolved magneto-terahertz spectroscopy, we demonstrate the ultrafast optical undressing of polarons in a Cd3As2 thin film. In equilibrium, a magnetic-field-induced spectral splitting near the 1.22-terahertz phonon mode reveals an 87% enhancement of the carrier effective mass due to the polaron effect. Upon photoexcitation, the enhanced carrier effective mass collapses within 5 ps, reflecting the transient undressing of this pre-existing polaronic state. Notably, this anomalous suppression contrasts sharply with prior studies where optical excitation exclusively triggers polaron formation in topological semimetals. This study provides deep insights into the ultrafast magneto-optical dynamics of pre-existing polarons, advancing the design of high-performance topological devices.
papers.tldr: Using time-resolved magneto-terahertz spectroscopy, researchers show that equilibrium polarons in a Cd₃As₂ thin film enhance the carrier effective mass by 87% and are ultrafast optically “undressed” within 5 ps upon photoexcitation.

papers.title: Air-Stable Nickel Oxide Nanosheets as a Model Platform for Decoupling Structure–Activity Relation in Oxygen Evolving Electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.
papers.tldr: Air-stable submonolayer NiO nanosheets on Au(111) provide an atomic-scale model platform showing that alkaline OER activity is governed by edge-site density, with edges forming active nickel oxyhydroxide species and offering a design rule to maximize accessible edge sites.

papers.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
authors: Jae-Mo Lihm, Malte R\"osner, Cyrus E. Dreyer, Massimiliano Stengel, Samuel Ponc\'e
papers.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The method handles entangled bands and accurately reproduces TDDFPT at a fraction of its cost. We use it to compute the total dynamical electron-electron interaction, including direct Coulomb and phonon-mediated interactions with dynamically screened electron-electron and electron-phonon couplings, all on equal footing. In hole-doped monolayer hBN, the hybridization of the carrier plasmon with the longitudinal optical phonon makes the low-energy retarded interaction nonmonotonic in the carrier density, an effect missed by the adiabatic approximation. In metallic monolayer TaS2, nonadiabatic effects are weak and occur only due to the intraband electron-hole continuum and the nesting of nearly parallel Fermi velocities. We also validate the widely used screened-screened approximation for the phonon spectral function. This work opens the way to first-principles studies of spectral functions, transport, and superconductivity with dynamically screened interactions.
papers.tldr: The paper introduces **DFPT+A downfolding**, a Wannier-based active-space first-principles method that efficiently computes dynamically screened electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions on equal footing at near-TDDFPT accuracy, revealing plasmon-phonon-driven nonmonotonic screening in hole-doped hBN and weak nonadiabatic effects in metallic TaS₂.

papers.title: Photodoping-Driven Lattice Expansion Enables Polarization Enhancement in Sliding Ferroelectric MoS2
papers.abstract: Abstract Light-matter interactions provide a powerful route to dynamically control ferroelectricity in low-dimensional materials, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing light-induced polarization remain elusive in sliding ferroelectrics. However, the influence of photodoped carriers on the macroscopic polarization and lattice responses remains largely unexplored. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to demonstrate the microscopic origin of the photostrictive response in rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 under carrier photodoping. The system exhibits a characteristic lattice deformation, including in-plane expansion with the magnitude of 2% under a moderate photodoping density, collectively enhancing electronic hybridization. The coupling gives rise to a substantial interlayer contraction and an increase in out-of-plane spontaneous polarization, accompanied by a softening of the interlayer vibrational mode. These results demonstrate a microscopic, nonthermal pathway for modulating ferroelectric properties and underscore the potential of lattice-engineered polarization control in two-dimensional sliding ferroelectrics for advanced optoelectronic and information storage technologies.
papers.tldr: First-principles calculations show that photodoping rhombohedral bilayer MoS₂ drives in-plane lattice expansion and interlayer contraction, enhancing out-of-plane sliding ferroelectric polarization via increased electronic hybridization and interlayer mode softening.

papers.title: Functional Charge-Transport Channels in Particle-Assembled Photoelectrodes: From Percolation to Interfacial Energetics
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abstract: Abstract Particle-assembled semiconductor photoelectrodes can integrate high-quality powders derived from high-temperature or solution synthesis into devices, yet random and loose interparticle contacts often cause severe majority-carrier collection losses. This Perspective presents a unified framework coupling physical network construction with electronic design. Its physical construction requires percolation at low material loading without excessively covering reactive surfaces or pores, while electronic design demands carrier selectivity, energetic continuity, and high conductivity. We unify surface-derived layers, second-phase networks, and vertical scaffolds within this framework, shifting the focus from materials selection to conductive channel engineering. We identify controlled structural characterization, operando carrier-pathway probing, and long-term stability as current challenges, and propose future research strategies. We argue that such channel construction and electronic design could become a key pathway for particle-assembled photoelectrodes to advance from materials toward efficient devices.
papers.tldr: This Perspective argues that particle-assembled photoelectrodes must jointly engineer percolating physical networks and electronically selective, energetically continuous conductive channels, shifting the focus from materials selection to conductive-channel engineering.

papers.title: The spin-transfer inverse Faraday effect in Au/YIG thin film bilayers
authors: Victor H. Ortiz, Daniel Russell, Fengyuan Yang, Roland K. Kawakami
papers.abstract: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. In metallic/ferromagnetic-insulator (NM/FMI) bilayers, IFE-driven spin polarization in the metallic layer can be an alternative to generate magnon excitations in the magnetic insulator which otherwise would be inaccessible with photon energies below the insulator bandgap, but this avenue has remained mostly unexplored. In this work, we investigate the regime of spin-transfer via IFE in Au/YIG bilayers, by means of ultrafast time-resolved magneto-optical experiments. Understanding the mechanism of this spin-transfer IFE in these NM/FMI heterostructures is crucial for several reasons: it elucidates the fundamental coupling between light's angular momentum and collective spin modes at buried interfaces, it enables all-optical generation and manipulation of pure spin currents, and it paves the way toward THz-frequency spintronic devices leveraging the insulator's long magnon lifetimes.
papers.tldr: This paper uses ultrafast time-resolved magneto-optical experiments to investigate inverse-Faraday-effect-driven spin transfer in Au/YIG bilayers, where circularly polarized light generates spin polarization in the Au layer that can excite magnons in the magnetic insulator YIG.

papers.title: Bipolar Redox Molecule-Assembled Freestanding Film Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries with Excellent Thermal Adaptivity and Ultralong Life
papers.abstract: Abstract Organic molecules with high redox potentials and large theoretical capacities are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by issues of dissolution, low electrical conductivity, and insufficient utilization of active sites. We report herein freestanding film cathodes for high-performance ZIBs with superior charge storage and heat management, wherein a meticulously designed bipolar redox molecule is assembled into a continuous three-dimensional conductive framework of MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotubes. The optimal cathode-based coin cells deliver the highest specific capacity of 406.6 mAh g–1 at 0.05 A g–1 and an initial capacity of 219.61 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1 with extraordinary cycling stability over 60,000 cycles with an average capacity decay of only 2.5 × 10–4% per cycle. Further cycling test at 55 °C and 3 A g–1 reveals an initial capacity of 252.15 mAh g–1 with over 82.75% retention after 3000 cycles and ∼100% coulombic efficiency. Importantly, thermal conductivity and infrared thermal imaging were employed for clear elaboration of temperature evolution dynamics and thermal distribution under different electrode structures. Our work correlating the structure design and thermal management of electrodes provides insights for the rational design of high-performance ZIBs.
papers.tldr: A bipolar redox molecule assembled into an MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotube freestanding film enables high-capacity, ultralong-life, and thermally adaptive aqueous zinc-ion battery cathodes with effective heat management.

papers.title: Realizing Reversible Photo‐Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS 2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo‐Rechargeable Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo‐assisted charging, whereas light‐only photo‐charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo‐charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo‐charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo‐charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS 2 by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS 2 . Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self‐discharge current and the photo‐charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn 2+ photo‐batteries that can be reversibly photo‐charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo‐rechargeable batteries could realize a photo‐charging capacity ratio of 100% by2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest‐conversion‐storage mini‐system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.
papers.tldr: A NiO-modified stacked 1T/2H MoS₂ bifunctional cathode with balanced photocharging/self-discharge currents enables genuine, reversible light-only photo-charging of Zn²⁺ photo-batteries for over ten cycles, achieving a 100% photo-charging capacity ratio and 110.55 mAh g⁻¹ for a practical energy harvest–conversion–storage mini-system.

papers.title: Temperature Evolution of Magnon-Polarons in the van der Waals Antiferromagnet FePS$_3$
authors: A. Krajewska, J. Kierdaszuk, M. Dub, E. Karpierz-Marczewska, M. Potemski
papers.abstract: Magnon polarons, hybrid excitations arising from magnon-phonon coupling, were investigated in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using magneto-Raman scattering measurements at temperatures ranging from 4 K to the vicinity of the N\'eel temperature ($T_\mathrm{N}$ = 118 K). The lower Zeeman-split component of the magnon-like mode, tuned by the magnetic field toward the lower-energy phonon mode, exhibits an avoided crossing. The corresponding magnetic field decreases from approximately 13 T at 4 K to 5.6 T at 85 K, bringing the effect within reach of a standard laboratory magnet. A model of three coupled bosonic modes shows that the magnon-phonon coupling constant, approximately 2.7 cm$^{-1}$ at low temperatures, decreases significantly with increasing temperature, following a trend similar to the temperature-induced softening of the magnon mode. This decrease in magnon-phonon coupling is discussed in terms of a possible reduction in sublattice magnetization due to thermal fluctuations.
papers.tldr: Magneto-Raman measurements in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS₃ reveal that magnon-polaron avoided crossings shift to lower magnetic fields with increasing temperature as the magnon-phonon coupling weakens alongside magnon softening, likely due to thermal reduction of sublattice magnetization.

papers.title: Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
authors: Fei Wang, Xuanxi Cai, Wanying Chen, Xiao Tang, Jinze Li, Benshu Fan, Tianshuang Sheng, Jinxi Lu, Jiansong Li, Hongyun Zhang, Pu Yu, Peizhe Tang, Wenhui Duan, Angel Rubio, Zhiyuan Sun, Shuyun Zhou
papers.abstract: Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamiltonian, strong optical fields offer a fundamentally different route by reshaping the Hamiltonian on ultrafast timescales, turning symmetry and topology into dynamically controllable degrees of freedom. Graphene provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing this concept, where circularly polarized light has long been predicted to dynamically break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and open a topologically nontrivial gap at the Dirac point. Despite extensive experimental efforts, direct observation of this Dirac gap-the defining spectroscopic signature of the dynamical TRS-breaking induced topological phase-has remained missing. Here we directly observe this light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the gap emerges simultaneously with the optical field and exclusively under circularly polarized driving, directly linking its opening to dynamical TRS breaking. Together with Floquet theory, we identify the gap with a light-induced Haldane mass and reveal the associated nontrivial Floquet Berry curvature and Chern topology. By demonstrating dynamical TRS breaking in a prototypical non-magnetic material, our results establish optical driving as a route to ultrafast engineering of symmetry and topology, opening opportunities for dynamically tunable quantum matter beyond equilibrium.
papers.tldr: Researchers directly observed a light-induced Haldane gap at the Dirac point of monolayer graphene using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy under circularly polarized driving, demonstrating dynamical time-reversal symmetry breaking and Floquet Chern topology.

papers.title: Finite-Depth Interfacial Coupling in Metal/Topological Insulator van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Abstract Metal/topological insulator van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures offer a platform for engineering emergent quantum states beyond isolated layers. While proximity effects in covalently bonded systems are well studied, coupling depth across vdW interfaces remains unclear. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, we investigate the thickness dependence of TiTe2/Bi2Te3 electronic states. Despite nominally weak vdW bonding, the buried interface induces emergent bands and splitting near a band crossing, consistent with hybridization. Interface-induced features persist in the bilayer, while band evolution nearly saturates in thicker films. Even at four layers, the electronic structure does not simply recover to the intrinsic TiTe2 limit, consistent with finite-depth coupling that substantially reshapes the overlayer bands. Charge redistribution and a moiré-modulated interfacial potential contribute to this reconstruction. Finite-depth coupling may be a hallmark of strongly coupled vdW heterostructures and guide topological and quantum electronic device design.
papers.tldr: In TiTe₂/Bi₂Te₃ van der Waals heterostructures, interfacial hybridization and charge/moiré effects create finite-depth electronic coupling that persists across several overlayer layers and prevents thicker films from recovering intrinsic TiTe₂ behavior.

papers.title: SPAD-Array Characterization of Biexciton Emission from Single Colloidal Quantum Shells
papers.abstract: Abstract Characterizing multiphoton emission is essential for understanding and developing quantum light sources. Emerging single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) array detectors offer new opportunities but require tailored analysis strategies. Here we present such approaches for colloidal nanoparticles with long-lived multiexciton states, where multiple bright excitonic and charged states contribute to emission. Using CdS/CdSe/CdS quantum shells as a model system, we combine high-throughput characterization across more than 1000 particles with state-resolved spectroscopy. Double projection of the sample image onto the detector prevents crosstalk artifacts and improves data quality. High-throughput photon-correlation measurements on a frame-based SPAD-array camera quantify biexciton emission efficiency and reveal particle-to-particle variations. Reference time-gated measurements distinguish individual particles from clusters. An event-based linear SPAD array resolves bimodal biexciton spectra but reveals no strong blue shift relative to the exciton, in contrast to previous reports. Our study presents insights into multiphoton emission by colloidal quantum shells and experimental strategies for quantum-emitter characterization.
papers.tldr: This study introduces tailored SPAD-array characterization strategies to measure biexciton emission from single colloidal CdS/CdSe/CdS quantum shells at high throughput, quantifying biexciton efficiency and particle-to-particle variation while resolving bimodal biexciton spectra and finding no strong blue shift relative to the exciton.

papers.title: Cation-Intercalated Mott Insulator α-RuCl3 Superlattice for Actively Tuned Optoelectronics
papers.abstract: Abstract Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by &gt;3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.
papers.tldr: Cation intercalation converts α-RuCl3 into a TMA+-intercalated Mott-insulator superlattice that narrows its optical gap to ~0.6 eV for short-wave infrared sensing and, with a van der Waals tunneling barrier, suppresses dark current and boosts detectivity for machine-learning-assisted image recognition.

papers.title: A Dual-Function Electrolyte Additive Suppresses Mn Crosstalk for Durable High-Temperature Graphite/LiMn2O4 Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Mn crosstalk accelerates the degradation of graphite/LiMn2O4 (LMO) batteries, particularly at elevated temperatures, through the migration and deposition of dissolved Mn species on the graphite anode, which destabilizes the anode interphase. Here, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) suppresses this cross-electrode degradation pathway by regulating both the bulk electrolyte chemistry and the LMO/electrolyte interface. In the bulk electrolyte, the Si–O groups of TMSP consume HF and suppress continued HF generation through LiPF6 hydrolysis, thereby weakening acid-induced LMO corrosion. At the cathode interface, preferential adsorption and oxidation of TMSP promote the formation of a thin (∼3 nm) Li3PO4-rich cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), which limits electrolyte decomposition and Mn dissolution. These complementary effects reduce Mn dissolution and deposition on the graphite anode, thereby limiting Mn-associated SEI growth and resistance increase. In 1.6 Ah graphite/LMO 18650 cells, 2.1 wt % TMSP reduces Mn deposition on the anode by 95.2% and increases capacity recovery from 90.5% to 95.1% after storage at 60 °C for 7 days. The cells also retain 80.2% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C and 45 °C. These results establish the suppression of Mn crosstalk as an effective strategy for improving the high-temperature durability of graphite/LMO batteries.
papers.tldr: A dual-function TMSP electrolyte additive suppresses Mn crosstalk in graphite/LiMn₂O₄ batteries by consuming HF and forming a Li₃PO₄-rich cathode interphase, thereby reducing Mn dissolution/deposition and improving high-temperature cycling and storage durability.

papers.title: Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
papers.abstract: Abstract High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.
papers.tldr: Ca₂CoN₂, a high-pressure-synthesized transition metal nitride, hosts an incommensurate double-k spin-density-wave order below 54 K that lies close to a predicted modulated spin-liquid instability, highlighting nitrides as model systems for complex frustrated magnetism.

papers.title: The Generalized Twin Image: Understanding Regularized Phase Retrieval
authors: Zhiyuan Hu, Michael Unser, Jonathan Dong
papers.abstract: Image priors can dramatically improve phase retrieval reconstruction, but their effectiveness strongly varies between imaging modalities. We introduce the generalized twin image, which extends the classical twin-image ambiguity from Fourier phase retrieval to any invertible sensing operator, to understand this effectiveness. The ambiguity extends to undersampled and oversampled measurements, remaining exact under undersampling and for oversampled coded Fourier measurements. We show that it provides a simple criterion to assess regularization effectiveness: the image prior should favor the ground truth over its generalized twin image. We propose the total-variation ratio as a simple measure of this preference, and derive closed-form estimates for structured random phase retrieval models. Experiments with a pretrained denoiser demonstrate that the ratio predicts regularized reconstruction performance across different sensing models.
papers.tldr: The paper introduces the generalized twin image to extend Fourier phase retrieval’s twin-image ambiguity to arbitrary invertible sensing operators and shows that a total-variation ratio between the ground truth and its generalized twin predicts how effectively image priors regularize phase retrieval reconstruction.

papers.title: Embracing Phase Transitions to Rationalize the High Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Nickel Selenides in Alkaline Electrolytes
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract The transformation of electrodeposited NiSe nanocatalysts was studied under oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions in alkaline electrolytes by a combination of operando X-ray absorption (XAS) and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The upper layers of nickel selenides transform into nickel oxide/oxyhydroxide species, which exhibit higher catalytic OER activity than the as-synthesized nickel oxide/oxyhydroxide, as reported previously. The coupled operando XAS and EIS experiments reveal that the Ni3+/Ni4+ transition occurs at lower potentials than the OER, involving a transient phase transformation at the foot of the nickel oxidation peak. Based on these findings and using insights from complementary operando (Raman spectroscopy, scanning flow cell inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry) and ex situ measurements (XAS and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy), a catalytic cycle is proposed within the framework of frustrated phase transitions linking the molecular transformation of substrate and products (H2O/O2) to structural and electronic changes of the solid catalyst (β-Ni(OH)2/β-NiOOH). Specifically, the Ni–O distance of the formed β-NiOOH surface species on top of the NiSe layers elongates, facilitating rapid local transitions between different catalyst phases and oxidation states, which are essential for rapid completion of the catalytic cycle under operando conditions.
papers.tldr: Operando XAS/EIS show that electrodeposited nickel selenides partially convert to β-NiOOH surface species with elongated Ni–O bonds, enabling rapid frustrated phase transitions between catalyst phases and oxidation states that rationalize their high alkaline oxygen evolution reaction activity.

papers.title: Chemical Coordination and Pore Confinement Enabling a Bifunctional Interface for Accelerated Desolvation and Oriented Deposition Toward Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage; however, dendrites formation and corrosion on zinc anodes significantly hinder their practical applications. Uneven Zn deposition leads to dendrite growth, while H 2 O molecules in solvated Zn 2+ ions exacerbate surface corrosion and the hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, we propose a Schiff‐base‐covalently‐grafted UiO‐66‐NH 2 metal‐organic framework to construct a bifunctional interface for stable zinc metal anodes. Specifically, the chemical chelation between Schiff base and Zn 2+ accelerates desolvation and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed Zn 2+ ‐chelated sites and the well‐defined confined pore channels of UiO‐66‐NH 2 scaffold guide a homogeneous Zn 2+ flux and promote Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. As a result, this bifunctional interface enables Zn plating/stripping with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% over 2000 cycles at 5 mA cm −2 /1 mAh cm −2 . Furthermore, it achieves a capacity retention of over 90% after 4000 charge–discharge cycles in a Zn||MnO 2 full cell. This work is expected to open a new avenue for interfacial chemical regulation toward stabilizing zinc metal anodes.
papers.tldr: A Schiff-base-covalently-grafted UiO-66-NH₂ bifunctional interface enables accelerated Zn²⁺ desolvation and homogeneous (002)-oriented Zn deposition, suppressing dendrites and corrosion for highly stable zinc metal anodes.

papers.title: Potentials of individual atoms by convergent beam electron diffraction
authors: Tatiana Latychevskaia, Colin Robert Woods, Yi Bo Wang, Matthew Holwill, Eric Prestat, Sara Mustafi, Sarah J. Haigh, Kostya S. Novoselov
papers.abstract: In convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) on two-dimensional (2D) materials, the intensity distributions within the individual CBED spots map the local atomic arrangements within the probed region. In this study we demonstrate that the average intensities within the CBED spots essentially depend on the scattering parameters by a single atom, thus, offering the possibility of the direct measurement of such parameters. Scattering potential of an individual atom can be approximated by the Gaussian function and its parameters, the standard deviation and the maximal phase shift, can be recovered from the ratio of the intensities in the zero- and higher orders spots in CBED pattern. In order to demonstrate this, we simulated CBED patterns and extracted the atomic scattering parameters from such patterns. In the simulated examples, no weak phase object approximation is applied and the proposed method provides accurate results even for materials with large phase shifts up to 1.5 rad, as for example tungsten. The scattering parameters recovered from the experimental CBED patterns of graphene and twisted graphene-hBN structure show good agreement with the theoretically obtained values.
papers.tldr: The paper shows that the ratio of intensities in zero- and higher-order convergent beam electron diffraction spots can directly recover the Gaussian scattering-potential parameters of individual atoms, demonstrated in simulations and in graphene and twisted graphene-hBN experiments.

papers.title: Controlling Redox Interplay in the Formation of Anisotropic Multimetallic Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Abstract Controlling the interplay between reduction and galvanic processes is critical for tailoring the structure and composition of multimetallic nanocrystals. Here, we report a synthetic strategy to produce anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions. Platinum deposition on single-crystal Au@Pd nanorods (NRs) was modulated by varying the concentration of ascorbic acid, enabling control over the balance between reduction and galvanic-like processes. This approach yields distinct nanostructures, including nanoframes, cloud-like morphologies, and core–shell–shell architectures. Advanced electron microscopy, including high-resolution HAADF STEM imaging, EDX elemental mapping, and electron tomography, reveals intricate elemental distributions, the formation of cavities and tunnels, the apparent preservation of single-crystal characteristics in Au@Pd NRs under the explored conditions, and gold etching induced by the platinum precursor. A preliminary evaluation of catalytic activity suggests enhanced ethanol oxidation performance for nanoframe structures. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering anisotropic multimetallic nanocrystals through controlled redox interplay.
papers.tldr: By tuning ascorbic acid to balance reduction and galvanic processes, researchers synthesize anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions, including catalytically promising nanoframes.

papers.title: Synchronous and Unidirectional Epitaxy of Layer‐Controlled Graphene on Oxidized Single‐Crystal Copper Wafers With Tunable Stacking Order
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The deterministic synthesis of wafer‐scale two‐dimensional (2D) materials with programmable layer number, crystallographic orientation, and stacking order is essential for unlocking their layer‐dependent quantum properties and enabling scalable device integration. Here, we demonstrate a synchronous and unidirectional epitaxy strategy for chemical vapor deposition growth of layer‐controlled graphene on atomically flat oxidized single‐crystal Cu wafers. Using a Cu(111)–Cu 2 O(111) heterogeneous catalytic substrate, we achieved 2‐inch single‐crystalline graphene films with precisely tunable layer numbers (2 to 5). By engineering the atomic steps of high‐index Cu surfaces, we created deterministic spatial patterning of alternating Bernal and rhombohedral stacking in trilayer graphene, as confirmed by near‐field nano‐optics and angle‐resolved photoemission spectroscopy. The resulting wafer‐scale films exhibit exceptional thickness uniformity, high crystallinity, and an ultra‐flat surface. This work provides a unified growth framework that concurrently resolves the intertwined challenges of layer control, wafer‐scale single crystallinity, and stacking order modulation, laying a material foundation for advanced device studies and potential applications.
papers.tldr: A synchronous, unidirectional epitaxy strategy on oxidized single-crystal Cu(111) wafers enables 2-inch single-crystalline graphene with tunable 2–5 layers and deterministically patterned Bernal/rhombohedral stacking.

papers.title: Uniaxial strain-induced multipiezo effect in two-dimensional multifunctional altermagnet Cr2X2O and Janus Cr2XYO
papers.abstract: Altermagnetism has attracted considerable attention in recent years. As an emerging magnetic phase, it features collinear antiferromagnetic order, yielding a zero net magnetic moment and nonrelativistic spin splitting. Using density functional theory, we reported five stable semiconducting altermagnetic monolayers: Cr2X2O and Janus Cr2XYO (X, Y = S, Se, Te, X ≠ Y). These monolayers exhibit C-paired spin–valley locking, strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy, a strain-tunable piezovalley response, and strain-induced magnetization assisted by carrier doping. Distinct from previously reported two-dimensional altermagnets, these five materials exhibit pronounced valley polarization under uniaxial strain, which primarily originates from the p orbitals of the chalcogen atoms. The out-of-plane piezoelectricity of Janus Cr2XYO monolayers arises from the electronegativity difference between the X and Y atoms. Among them, Cr2Te2O exhibits the largest valley polarization of 222 meV under −4% uniaxial strain, while Cr2STeO exhibits a sizable out-of-plane piezoelectric response with a d31 coefficient of 0.63 pm/V. Our results reveal a multipiezo effect in Cr2X2O and Janus Cr2XYO monolayers that integrates spin, valley, and mechanical degrees of freedom, thereby establishing a multifunctional material system for valleytronics, spintronics, and flexible piezoelectric devices.
papers.tldr: Density functional theory identifies five stable semiconducting 2D altermagnets, Cr₂X₂O and Janus Cr₂XYO, in which uniaxial strain induces a multipiezo effect coupling spin, valley, and mechanical degrees of freedom for valleytronics, spintronics, and flexible piezoelectric applications.

papers.title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. Once insulating sulfides become poorly connected to the electronic network, charge recovery becomes incomplete and cathode passivation rapidly accumulates. Here, we construct chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces by embedding Fe 3 C–MnO heteropoints within nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon nanotubes. The heterointerface integrates carbon‐side electronic coupling, sulfide‐side affinity, and interfacial polarization, thereby suppressing localized sulfide accumulation and sustaining charge‐stage sulfur recovery as mechanical confinement weakens. This effect is strongly pressure dependent. Under high compression, the electrochemical responses of different hosts converge, whereas under contact‐limited conditions the Fe 3 C–MnO architecture preserves markedly higher sulfur utilization, lower polarization, and superior cycling stability. Consequently, the operational pressure required to retain ≥80% of the 10 MPa discharge capacity decreases from approximately 2 MPa for the control cathodes to 0.2 MPa for Fe 3 C–MnO/NC@S. A 200 µm cathode with 8.3 mg cm −2 sulfur sustains reversible cycling at 0.2 MPa, together with a pouch‐cell energy density of 696 Wh kg cathode −1 . These results establish sulfide‐interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.
papers.tldr: Embedding Fe₃C–MnO heteropoints in N-doped hollow carbon nanotubes creates chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces that preserve sulfur conversion and charge recovery under contact-limited conditions, enabling thick solid-state Na–S cathodes to cycle at 0.2 MPa with high sulfur utilization and 696 Wh kg_cathode⁻¹.

papers.title: Current-driven transient dynamics of magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: Current-driven magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for fast spintronic devices, yet their transient dynamics are not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate spin-orbit-torque-driven domain-wall motion in Mn$_\text{3}$Sn using a multipole micromagnetic framework. The three symmetry-related 60{\deg} walls exhibit equivalent current-driven dynamics, unlike their field-driven motion. For a representative 60{\deg} wall, the post-pulse motion is governed by relaxation of the current-induced rotation of the surrounding octupole domains, with a characteristic time of approximately 33 ps quantitatively captured by a uniform-domain analytic model. By resolving spatially nonuniform texture dynamics beyond this analytic description, the simulations further reveal an additional slow relaxation in a composite 180{\deg} wall associated with the relative motion of its constituent walls. The post-pulse response also varies systematically with the exchange stiffness and magnetic anisotropies. These results identify distinct domain and internal-coordinate relaxation channels and establish the intrinsic time scales governing pulse-controlled positioning of magnetic-octupole domain walls in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.
papers.tldr: Using multipole micromagnetics, the paper shows that current-driven magnetic-octupole domain walls in Mn₃Sn exhibit post-pulse relaxation governed by current-induced rotation of surrounding octupole domains (~33 ps for 60° walls), while composite 180° walls add a slower internal-coordinate relaxation mode, revealing distinct time scales for pulse-controlled domain-wall positioning in antiferromagnetic spintronics.

papers.title: Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling
authors: Vsevolod Biryukov, Sergey V. Barabash, Pranab Kumar Das, Jack Deslippe, Mauro Del Ben, Felipe H. da Jornada, Yuming Shi, Johannes Voss, Zhenglu Li, Piero Altoe, Kamal Choudhary, Ruth Pachter, Steven G. Louie, Marvin L. Cohen, Timur Bazhirov
papers.abstract: Quantum-mechanical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), underpin much of modern computational materials science and are the primary source of data for AI-driven discovery. Yet the established electronic-structure codes today represent decades-old software architectures, making new physical models slow and costly to implement, validate, and deploy on emerging hardware. We present Quantum 3xplorer (Q3, pronounced "Quantum Explorer"), an AI-native quantum simulation engine written from scratch by AI coding agents under the direction and supervision of domain scientists. As a first and demanding validation case, we implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT end to end: norm-conserving, ultrasoft, and projector-augmented-wave formalisms, spin polarization, DFT+U, and dispersion corrections, together with forces, stresses, structural relaxation, and electronic-structure analysis. Q3 reproduces established reference implementations, runs faster on a single core in representative benchmarks, and scales across GPU-accelerated supercomputers. It was developed in weeks rather than years. Its layered, physics-first architecture separates abstract quantum-mechanical concepts from their numerical representations, making its framework extendable beyond plane waves to other basis sets and levels of theory. Its inputs and outputs follow structured, schema-validated data standards, making every result AI-ready. Q3 is open source under Apache 2.0 and built to be reused, extended, and improved by the research community. Q3 points to a paradigm shift in how computational quantum science is done. Scientists define the physics, formulate the models, and set the criteria for validation; AI agents write, test, and optimize the code. The decades-long path from a new theory to a trusted, high-performance implementation can thus collapse to days, significantly accelerating scientific discovery.
papers.tldr: Quantum 3xplorer (Q3) is an open-source, AI-native plane-wave DFT simulation engine written by AI coding agents under human scientific supervision that reproduces reference results and scales on HPC/GPU systems, demonstrating how AI-driven development can compress quantum-method implementation from years to weeks.
